item.title: Supporting the Safe Electrification of Small Craft with EN ISO 16315:2026
item.description: The transition towards electric and hybrid propulsion is reshaping the small-craft sector. Boatbuilders and equipment manufacturers are increasingly deploying advanced propulsion architectures that combine batteries, power electronics, electric motors, generators and control systems to deliver lower-emission and more energy-efficient vessels. As these technologies evolve, ensuring their safe and reliable integration becomes increasingly important. EN ISO 16315:2026 addresses this need by providing a dedicated framework for the design and installation of electrical systems used for propulsion in small craft. item.title: CRA Milestone Unlocked: First European standards supporting CRA are now available!
item.description: CEN and CENELEC have reached an important milestone in supporting the implementation of the European Cyber Resilience Act (CRA), with the publication of two new European Standards: EN 40000-1-1 on cybersecurity terminology and EN 40000-1-2 on cybersecurity principles, product risk management and lifecycle activities. These are among the first standards developed under Standardization Request M/606, through which the European Commission has asked the European Standardization Organizations, CEN, CENELEC and ETSI, to develop standards supporting the implementation of the CRA. The CRA introduces a common European framework for the cybersecurity of products with digital elements, covering a wide range of hardware and software products. item.title: New Harmonized Standards for Aviation Ground Support Equipment: EN 1915-2 and EN 12312-20
item.description: After more than 15 years, two important standards for aviation ground support equipment (GSE) have been comprehensively revised and republished, replacing editions that had been in force since 2009. The new standards provide updated requirements for the design, testing, and operation of equipment used in airport ground handling activities. As a result, manufacturers, designers, testing laboratories, and operators should review the changes and assess their impact on product compliance and operational practices. The standards form part of two complementary series developed by CEN/TC 274 ‘Aircraft Ground Support Equipment’. item.description: A new CEN Workshop is being planned as part of the activities of the EU project 'Caring Nature'. item.title: The updated CEN-CENELEC Guide 36 is now available
item.description: CEN and CENELEC have published the revised CEN-CENELEC Guide 36,‘Guidance on the rules for the drafting and presentation of candidate performance harmonized standards in support of Regulation (EU) 2024/3110 Construction Products Regulation CPR-2024’, following its approval by the CEN and CENELEC Technical Boards. The Guide is intended for Technical Committees developing candidate performance harmonized European Standards for construction products. It provides guidance on the drafting and presentation of standards developed in response to a standardization request issued under Regulation (EU) 2024/3110 (CPR-2024), in accordance with Article 5 of the Regulation. item.title: Draft CWA for comment: 'Green and Circular Healthcare Buildings: Circularity, Energy, and Wellbeing'
item.description: A new CEN Workshop is being planned as part of the activities of the EU project 'Caring Nature'. This project focuses its energies on reducing the carbon footprint of the healthcare sector. This is no small task, and many innovative solutions are needed that consider the safety and health of both patients and operators. In the area of healthcare buildings, there is a current lack of standardized principles and guidelines for circularity and green practices. At the same time there is growing demand for healthcare infrastructure that is environmentally sustainable. To meet this challenge, a CEN Workshop has been proposed. The Workshop is tasked with helping to develop a Green Circular Compass – a tool which will take into account several areas, including circularity, energy, and well-being.

item.title: European Agile Specifications: a new step in modernizing European standardization
item.description: European standardization is evolving. New technologies, changing regulatory and market needs and increasingly digital ways of working require a system that can respond faster, while safeguarding the quality, consensus, openness and trust on which it is built. Against this backdrop, CEN and CENELEC have approved the European Agile Specification (EAS) – a new standardization deliverable designed to bring trusted technical solutions to market more quicky. The decision represents another concrete step in CEN and CENELEC’s ongoing work to modernize the European Standardization System and make it more responsive.
